directive:
Single revision directive: Preserve `thm:two-sided-risk-calibration` as the flagship kernel—especially its low-risk YES construction and unrestricted all-design/all-estimator NO lower bound—and do not add assumptions, replace risk by a graph proxy, or conceal the exact-regularization and design-adaptive Le Cam/dual crux. Make `κ_DTE(d)` deterministic by defining it as the infimum of deterministic `a ≥ 1` for which some randomized polynomial-time `A` satisfies, uniformly for every `n` and `G ∈ 𝒢_{n,d}`,

    Pr_A[Risk₂(Ψ_A(G),G) ≤ U_A(G) ≤ a R₂(G)] ≥ 2/3,

and state this same joint event in the hardness and frontier theorems. Add a separate, procedure-free numerical-value hardness corollary: no randomized polynomial-time `B` can uniformly output `Ṙ(G)` with

    Pr_B[R₂(G) ≤ Ṙ(G) ≤ d^(1/2−ε) R₂(G)] ≥ 2/3.

Derive it explicitly from the existing promise gap `R₂(G) ≤ C√d/n` in YES and `R₂(G) ≥ cd/[n(log d)^O(1)]` in NO, including median amplification and threshold/majority bookkeeping. Describe this only as a conditional resolution of [Conjecture 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.04909v1) under the stated one-sided upper-value approximation convention and the existing UGC and `NP ⊄ BPP` premises; remove every unqualified claim that the certificate-aware frontier itself proves the conjecture. If “multiplicative approximation” is instead intended symmetrically, do not claim the half-degree numerical corollary—the present gap supports only a quarter-degree exponent—and confine the headline to certificate-aware approximation. Finally, relabel the empty-network proposition as an already-known sanity check and use the defined `r=2` construction coherently: it yields independent Bernoulli(1/4) assignment with the modified desired-event HT estimator and order `n⁻¹` risk; do not invoke undefined `r=1` or claim Bernoulli(1/2).

Single revision directive: Repair the procedure information set by modeling recorded randomization explicitly: let a procedure use a joint law `Q` on design coins `ω` and assignment `z`, with estimator `γ(ω,z,Y(z))`; for CGD take `ω=W`, so every `E*_{i,k}` is observable from the retained design record, and never claim it is recoverable from `z`. Add the Rao–Blackwell/Jensen bridge showing that averaging `γ` over `Q(ω | z)` produces a `z`-only estimator with no larger squared risk for every schedule, hence the recorded-coin and original unrestricted minimax values are equal and the benchmark remains exactly `R₂(G)`; update the procedure, risk, algorithm-output, and `κ` types coherently without asserting a nonexistent derandomization of modified HT. In `def:mis-game`, replace the unbound-`k` condition by the two simultaneous constraints `n⁻¹∑ᵢu_{i,0}² ≤ 1` and `n⁻¹∑ᵢu_{i,1}² ≤ 1`, and state the exact bridge to `R₂(G)` used by the reduction. Demote the CGD upper to an explicitly already-known calibration proposition, citing Kandiros–Pipis–Daskalakis–Harshaw (2024), Algorithm 1, Proposition 3.5, and Theorem 4.1 for the recorded-randomization modified-HT construction, unbiasedness, and spectral variance bound, together with Kandiros–Harshaw–Sävje (2026), Corollary 1.1 and Section 5.1 for the regular-DTE `√(d+1)/n` lower benchmark; present the `O(√d)` certified upper only as their direct combination. Narrow all novelty language accordingly: Kandiros–Harshaw–Sävje already supplies the unrestricted MIS-game representation and network-specific design-adaptive mixture machinery, while the genuinely new kernel is the donor-promise-specific, exact-regular, DTE-realizable two-sided value separation—low-risk YES versus an all-design/all-estimator high-risk NO on the same reduction image—obtained by instantiating that machinery. Preserve verbatim in substance the deterministic uniform `Pr[Risk₂ ≤ U ≤ aR₂] ≥ 2/3` definition and the honest procedure-free one-sided numerical-hardness result and amplification bookkeeping. Add no assumptions, substitute no proxy for `R₂`, and do not weaken the unrestricted-estimator NO statement.

Single root directive: Replace the existential `T` lemma and every “instantiate the machinery” placeholder with a construction-and-witness dossier. Given donor `J` and reduction coins, explicitly define the labeled vertex set and exhaustive edge predicate of the output network `G`; give the exact regularization algorithm, including simplicity, parity and multiplicity handling, formulas implying `d = Δ^(2+o(1))` and `n = poly(m,Δ)`, polynomial runtime, success probability, and proofs that both completeness structure and the all-large-sets soundness invariant survive. Do not cite Austrin–Khot–Safra as supplying this step: their construction passes through an unbounded regular multigraph, samples edges, and deletes edges incident to high-degree vertices, leaving only a maximum-degree graph ([Theorem 4.1, Steps 1–3](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v007a003/v007a003.pdf)). Likewise, do not identify the Chalermsook–Laekhanukit–Nanongkai product with the target: its regular result starts from an already-regular independent-set instance under different hypotheses and produces an abstract bipartite induced-matching product, not a DTE conflict graph or risk separation ([Section 5.2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.4129)). For the constructed `G`, enumerate all vertical, cross-layer, treated-layer, and absent control-layer adjacencies and prove that the graph used by the reduction is exactly `H_DTE(G)`. Map each donor completeness independent set to an explicit distribution over realizable assignments/exposure sets, specify the recorded-coin estimator and inclusion probabilities, and calculate its `C√d/n` worst-case risk. On the same reduction image, write an explicit layerwise-normalized least-favourable mixture or dual witness and derive, for an arbitrary assignment law and arbitrary measurable estimator, the `cd/[n(log d)^K]` lower bound through stated posterior-risk, total-variation, or dual inequalities. Include a nondegenerate finite worked example—or a matched finite YES/NO pair—with complete vertex and edge lists, degree table, `H_DTE` adjacency/exposure check, realized assignments, and numerical YES-risk and NO-Bayes-risk calculations. If these objects cannot be exhibited, retract the frontier rather than encoding them as an assumption or continuing to postulate `T`. Preserve the recorded-coin/Rao–Blackwell bridge, separate layer moment constraints, already-known CGD calibration, deterministic uniform `≥2/3` joint-event definition of `κ`, and honest one-sided numerical-hardness convention; add no crux assumption, risk proxy, or restriction of the unrestricted-estimator NO kernel.

develop the explicit primal–dual formulation for the exact identity `R₂(G)=𝔅R₂(H_DTE(G))`; prove weak duality and assignment-law realizability with separate layer moment constraints; obtain an actual lower-risk certificate, allowing exponential size generally but proving compression for a clearly stated structural subclass; validate primal and dual on a nondegenerate exact example. Keep universal polynomial-size or constant-factor certification as an open question unless proved. Do not reintroduce the frontier, exact degree filling, hardness claims, or independence-number proxies.

> Replace the flagship with an exact saddle theorem for the full equal block-clique family \(G_{b,s}\), \(b\ge1,s\ge2\). Starting from the published exact MIS identity only as calibration, prove by block/unit symmetrization—without assuming unbiasedness or linearity—that the infimum over all assignment laws and all measurable estimators admits an optimal invariant procedure parameterized by a law on \(c=0,\ldots,b\) all-control blocks, uniform conditional on \(c\) over block choices and singleton treated labels. Reduce the exact risk to the constant-block-mean, between-block zero-sum, and within-block treated-contrast modes; solve that reduced game to an explicit value \(V_{b,s}\) (closed form or an explicitly solved finite convex program), give the realizing assignment law and estimator, and construct an atomwise-feasible finite prior supported on explicit symmetry orbits whose posterior risk is at least \(V_{b,s}\) for every one of the \(b+1\) MIS orbits and equals it on active orbits. This lower witness must certify all measurable estimators and all designs, and the upper and lower values must match; verify \(V_{1,s}=1\). Demote the published primal identity, realizability, posterior-mean weak duality, and orbit counting to cited calibration lemmas. State that Kandiros–Harshaw–Sävje already imply only \(\Theta(1/b)\), that Gabler (1990; ebook 2012) already covers randomized invariant minimax sampling without an unbiasedness premise and quadratic parameter spaces, and that Rinott (2009) already treats joint sampling-estimation strategies and Bayesian minimax calculations; claim novelty only for the conflict-constrained two-layer block-clique saddle and its explicit finite certificate.
